summary: LoadBoard queries the orphaned 0001 tables (board_cells/board_cell_tracks/tracks) that the curation path never writes, so a Postgres-backed server never restores its attached board on restart.
code: FROM board_cells bc LEFT JOIN board_cell_tracks bct ... LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.id = bct.track_id WHERE bc.session_id = $1
scenario: Admin builds a board via the builder (writes only board_tracks/board_layout_cells/board_layout_cell_tracks in migration 0002) and AttachBoard sets game_sessions.board_id. Server restarts. engine.Run (engine.go:212) calls LoadBoard(sessionID), which reads board_cells — a table nothing ever INSERTs into (grep: no INSERT INTO board_cells/board_cell_tracks/tracks anywhere in server/). LoadBoard returns 'no board', e.board stays nil, and the game boots with no board despite the durable board_id link. Auto-reload is dead; an admin must manually re-attach after every restart.
suggested_fix: Reload from the 0002 layout tables via the session's board_id (join game_sessions.board_id -> board_layout_cells/board_layout_cell_tracks/board_tracks, i.e. reuse LoadBoardByID keyed on the attached board_id), or drop the dead 0001 board_cells/board_cell_tracks/tracks tables and repoint LoadBoard.

summary: io.ReadAll on the LRCLIB response body has no size cap; a huge/malicious response OOMs the server (the 8s timeout bounds hang, not body size).
scenario: LRCLIB is an external HTTPS endpoint (default lrclib.net, overridable via YFI_LRCLIB_URL — operator config, so not an attacker-controlled SSRF vector, but MITM or a compromised/malicious mirror is in the conference threat model). A response that streams multi-GB (or an infinite chunked body inside the 8s window) is fully buffered into memory. HasSyncedLyrics is called per-track during a bulk board rescan, amplifying the blast radius across many concurrent fetches.
suggested_fix: Wrap the body: io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxLyricsBytes)) with a sane cap (e.g. 1 MiB) and reject/truncate beyond it.

summary: board_layout_cell_tracks PK is (board_id,row,col,track_id); the schema does not enforce the documented 'a track can only be in one cell per board' invariant that app queries assume.
code: PRIMARY KEY (board_id, row, col, track_id)  -- comment above claims one-cell-per-board
scenario: PlaceTrack (admin_store.go:202) upserts on (board_id,row,col,track_id). Two concurrent PlaceTrack calls (or sequential placements) for the same track into different (row,col) both succeed — the DB only dedups within an identical cell. UnplacedTracks' 'id NOT IN (SELECT track_id ...)' and the layout loaders then treat a doubly-placed track inconsistently, so a track can appear in two board cells with no DB guard.
suggested_fix: Add UNIQUE(board_id, track_id) so a track can be placed in at most one cell per board, and have PlaceTrack move rather than duplicate on conflict.

summary: GetBoard detects 'not found' by matching err.Error() == "no rows in result set" instead of errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) — brittle to any wrapping or lib message change.
code: if err.Error() == "no rows in result set" { return nil, nil }
scenario: Works today because pgx v5 QueryRow.Scan returns pgx.ErrNoRows unwrapped, whose message is exactly that string. If the query path ever wraps the error, or pgx changes the message, the sentinel check silently misses and GetBoard returns a hard 500 for a legitimately-absent board (callers in layout.go treat non-nil err as InternalServerError instead of 404). pgx.ErrNoRows is already imported in the package (repo_postgres.go:193) but unused here.
suggested_fix: Use errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) to detect the empty result.

summary: AdminSecret/NonceSecret/JoinSecret fall back to hardcoded defaults ('changeme-admin', 'dev-nonce-secret', 'dev-join-secret') with no production guard — the server boots silently with known secrets. (LOCKED contract file — report only.)
code: AdminSecret: env("ADMIN_SECRET", "changeme-admin"), NonceSecret: env("YFI_NONCE_SECRET", "dev-nonce-secret"), JoinSecret: env("YFI_JOIN_SECRET", "dev-join-secret")
scenario: A production deploy that forgets to set ADMIN_SECRET boots with 'changeme-admin'. At a hacker conference an attacker guesses/knows the default and gains admin (issue admin.* actions), and forges nonces with the public 'dev-nonce-secret'. No log warning, no refusal to start — the degradation is silent.
suggested_fix: config.go is locked, so gate at the caller (main.go): if any secret still equals its dev default and a prod flag/env (e.g. YFI_ENV=prod) is set, log.Fatal at boot. Note in CONTRACT-QUESTION that config.go should ideally return an error on default secrets in prod.
